transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-12
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lina Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rey (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM), Alex Ramos (Clearwave GC), Priya Nair (Clearwave Procurement), Samir Desai (Clearwave Platform), Marta Lopez (Clearwave InfoSec)
Links shared: pricing deck (tinyurl.com/rwd-pricing-cta), security packet (tinyurl.com/rwd-secpack), sample workload csv (drive/clearwave-samples)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement preflight to resolve MSA/DPA redlines, confirm SLA tiers, validate KMS/egress constraints, and agree next steps for pilot pricing and technical sandbox.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we, we put this in the calendar as a preflight, just to make sure legal and procurement are aligned before we, uh, send a formal MSA.
[00:12] Alex Ramos: Yep thanks Lina. Alex here from legal. We got the redline from procurement yesterday, a couple of fee questions and a DPA ask, so want to make sure we don't miss anything.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya on procurement. Budget windows closing end of July so we, we need pricing and committed tier to be clear.
[00:30] Marcus Rey: Cool, Marcus from Redwood infra. I'll run through the technical constraints, where costs come from, and options for VPC/private deployment vs hosted.
[00:40] Samir Desai: Samir - quick note, our platform has a weird token distribution - lots of short queries but heavy peak at end of day. So latency matters.
[00:51] Marta Lopez: Marta here - InfoSec quick: SOC2 is required, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained for 365 days, and egress restrictions for PHI.
[01:05] Lina Chen: Right so two high-level paths: 1) Hosted with encryption-at-rest and customer-managed KMS via our integration, or 2) Private (VPC) deploy where you run the inference in your VPC and we keep a control plane. Each has different SLA and pricing profiles.
[01:25] Alex Ramos: On MSA redlines: Clause 7.2 around indemnity, we asked to tighten language for data handling - specifically we need explicit commitments around not retaining PHI and proper deletion.
[01:38] Marcus Rey: On retention we do prefix/kv cache eviction, but note that on hosted the control plane can keep metadata for billing. We can opt-in to not keep logs for specific routes, though that, uh, impacts debugging.
[01:52] Priya Nair: Egress fees: procurement flagged unclear egress charges for embeddings export. Is that a per-GB fee? How is it broken down?
[02:05] Marcus Rey: Good question - on hosted it's charged as outbound data transfer plus token-processing. For embeddings export we'd typically show it as data egress (GB) plus per-embedding unit cost. We can add a line item in the quote.
[02:22] Alex Ramos: Also need clarity on SLAs. We asked for 99.9 latency SLO at p95 - is that for dedicated only?
[02:34] Lina Chen: 99.9 uptime SLA is available for Redwood Dedicated. For hosted we publish performance profiles but the contractual SLA is lower. For mission-critical we recommend Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool.
[02:48] Samir Desai: If we go Dedicated, does the model version pinning exist? We can't have silent model swaps.
[02:56] Marcus Rey: Yes, Dedicated supports pinned model versions and explicit rollout controls: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. We'll include the model pinning clause in the playbook doc.
[03:10] Marta Lopez: KMS specifics: will Redwood hold keys or integrate with our cloud KMS (we use GCP KMS)? What about HSM?
[03:21] Marcus Rey: We support customer-managed keys via GCP KMS or AWS KMS; HSM via partner integrations is possible for Private. On hosted we never hold the plaintext keys; encryption at rest managed by your KMS when configured.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Procurement also wants an exit/transition clause — if we stop, what's the data egress window and fees?
[03:45] Lina Chen: Standard exit: export window 30 days with assistance; egress fees apply at published rates but we can add a 15% credit for churn in the first year as a commercial concession.
[03:58] Alex Ramos: Can you put that concession in writing in the MSA? We need specific language to approve.
[04:05] Lina Chen: Yes we'll add a commercial appendix with the concession, and we'll mark it as time-limited.
[04:12] Jordan Patel: Quick note from CSM side - for pilots we typically do a 3 month pilot with a consumption cap, plus a sandbox with reduced logging for debug.
[04:23] Priya Nair: On pricing: procurement would prefer committed monthly spend with tiered discounts. Is there a minimum commit?
[04:33] Lina Chen: Common pattern: 3-month min for pilot with commit options; for Dedicated we have monthly reserved capacity starting at 2x A100 equivalent. We can map to your projected token volumes.
[04:45] Samir Desai: I'll share our token distribution CSV after the call. That should help you map commit to capacity.
[04:51] Marcus Rey: Perfect. Also a technical caveat: quantization reduces memory but can affect accuracy for some fine-tuned models; we'll mark recommended quant profiles.
[05:05] Alex Ramos: On legalese, data processor vs controller — for our use, Clearwave is controller, Redwood is processor. That mapping is fine but we need explicit subprocessor list.
[05:16] Lina Chen: We'll append our subprocessors and can provide SOC2 reports. We'll also provide a DPA appendix that lists subprocessors, retention, and deletion controls.
[05:28] Marta Lopez: One more - audit logs retention for 365 days is required, but logs must be exportable to our SIEM without extra fee.
[05:38] Marcus Rey: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM (via Pub/Sub or Kinesis) — there's an event export feature; we normally include it in enterprise plans. There might be a modest integration fee but can include it in the quote as waived for pilot.
[05:53] Priya Nair: Regarding pricing workbook, procurement wants line items: committed GPU hours, per-token price, per-embedding price, egress GB, and integration/setup.
[06:05] Lina Chen: We'll produce that workbook and a worked example for your monthly profile.
[06:14] Alex Ramos: Two legal asks to close: 1) Add the 30-day export window with explicit egress rates and the 15% first-year churn credit, 2) Add deletion verification step and right-to-audit clause with scope limited to our data only.
[06:32] Lina Chen: Agreed. We'll add deletion verification language and limited audit right (reasonable notice, scoped access).
[06:41] Samir Desai: One tangent - we might need a VPC-only path for PHI routes. Can we route PHI traffic to a private deployment and keep the rest on hosted?
[06:52] Marcus Rey: Yes, smart routing is supported — requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region). You could carve PHI routes into Dedicated or Private while keeping non-PHI on hosted.
[07:05] Priya Nair: Procurement will want price for hybrid routing.
[07:10] Lina Chen: We'll include a hybrid pricing scenario.
[07:15] Alex Ramos: Regarding liability caps — procurement asked for a higher cap for security incidents involving PHI. What's Redwood's standard?
[07:25] Lina Chen: Standard is 1x annual fees; enterprise exceptions can be negotiated with insurance proof. We'll flag that for legal review.
[07:36] Alex Ramos: Ok please attach insurer certs if you want to increase the cap.
[07:41] Marcus Rey: Noted.
[07:43] Jordan Patel: Quick ops question — who will be our day-1 contact for incident triage?
[07:48] Lina Chen: CSM (Jordan) will be primary, SE (Marcus) for technical triage, and we can set up an on-call rotation for enterprise customers.
[07:57] Marta Lopez: On data residency — Clearwave needs EU residency for EU patient data. Is that supported?
[08:06] Marcus Rey: We support region pinning in Dedicated and hosted with region-specific deployments; for EU residency we'll propose region routing and dedicated capacity in eu-west.
[08:18] Priya Nair: Can you confirm backup retention policies for that region?
[08:24] Marcus Rey: Backups follow region defaults; we can set retention to 90 days or as required. We'll note this in the security packet.
[08:36] Alex Ramos: Any third-party subprocessors in Europe?
[08:40] Lina Chen: We'll provide full subprocessor list and include EU data transfer mechanisms in the DPA.
[08:48] Priya Nair: Procurement also asked whether there's a penalty or credit if SLA misses happen during pilot.
[08:55] Lina Chen: For pilot we typically include a service credit schedule for missed uptime targets scaled to committed spend; we can add that into the pilot appendix.
[09:07] Samir Desai: Tech check: what is the expected p95 latency for embeddings on Dedicated with our token profile?
[09:14] Marcus Rey: Roughly 80-120ms per request for short sequences on a dedicated A100-like pool, depends on batching; we'll produce a worked example with your CSV.
[09:26] Alex Ramos: Great. Final thought from legal: redline for deletion verification - what evidence do you provide?
[09:34] Marcus Rey: We provide deletion confirmation logs and a signed attestation from our ops team; for extra assurance we can include a one-time attestation from your audit scope.
[09:46] Priya Nair: Ok procurement will expect that in writing.
[09:50] Lina Chen: Next steps recap: we'll send the redlined MSA/DPA with the commercial appendix including the 15% churn credit and export window; Marcus will send the sandbox runbook and perf deck; Samir will share token profile; Marta will send SOC2 artefacts list.
[10:10] Alex Ramos: Thanks, that works. We'll aim to review the MSA within 5 business days.
[10:16] Jordan Patel: I'll set up the follow-up meeting for the week of 2026-07-20 to go over SOC2 and pilot onboarding.
[10:24] Lina Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the packet.

End of transcript.
